name: Arpan Paul
current_role: Executive Chairman, SAJ Food Products Pvt Ltd (Bisk Farm), Kolkata
profile: Arpan Paul heads SAJ Food Products, the Kolkata-based maker of Bisk Farm biscuits founded in 2000 by his father Krishnadas Paul, who launched it at age 60. Arpan took over as executive chairman after his father's death in 2020; the company has been reported at roughly Rs 2,000+ crore turnover.
interesting_fact: His father Krishnadas Paul started SAJ Food at age 60 after suffering a Rs 15 crore business loss, and grew Bisk Farm into one of eastern India's leading biscuit brands.
deep_cut_fact: The company name SAJ comes from the initials of Krishnadas Paul's three children - Sharmistha, Arpan and Jayeeta - so Arpan's own initial is in the company name.
notes: Low media profile; few interviews found. Best route is via the company (Bisk Farm news/press section: https://www.biskfarm.com/news-media/press-release/).

name: Bhupinder Singh Manhas
current_role: Founder, Harman Finochem Ltd (Mumbai/Aurangabad API manufacturer); not listed among current board directors
profile: Bhupinder Singh Minhas (also spelled Manhas) founded Harman Finochem in 1983, an Indian maker and exporter of active pharmaceutical ingredients and intermediates (45+ APIs, 75+ countries served). The company is now run by family directors Harpreet Singh Minhas and Dr. Gurpreet Singh Minhas; he is presented on the company site as founder.
interesting_fact: Harman Finochem, which he founded in 1983, makes 45+ APIs including 10+ WHO essential medicines and supplies 75+ nations, with approvals from regulators such as Health Canada and Mexico's COFEPRIS.
deep_cut_fact: The company website quotes him as founder: 'At Harman Finochem, our work is guided by a simple principle: to foster health, happiness, and harmony in every life we touch, while staying true to our responsibility towards humanity.'
notes: Name spelled 'Minhas' on company site. He does not appear among current registered directors (Inderjit Kaur, Harpreet, Gurpreet, Savreen Minhas), so he may have retired or passed away - status unverified. Very low public profile; approach via company.

name: Si Xiaodong
current_role: Co-founder (and long-time executive director) of SRE Group Ltd, Shanghai property developer (HKEX: 1207, delisted Feb 2025); current role unverified
profile: Si Xiao Dong co-founded Shanghai real-estate developer SRE Group with her husband Shi Jian; the group built residential, office and commercial projects in Shanghai and listed in Hong Kong. She served as an executive director overseeing public relations. Control of SRE later passed to China Minsheng Investment and the shares were delisted in 2025.
interesting_fact: Before co-founding SRE, she spent 1986-1991 at Shanghai Garment Import and Export Company, handling trade with the United States.
deep_cut_fact: She graduated from the Faculty of Foreign Languages at Sichuan University, and ran SRE's public relations department as an executive director.
notes: Spelled 'Si Xiao Dong' in HKEX filings. Shares wealth listing with husband Shi Jian. SRE was suspended and delisted (Feb 2025); no current public contact route found. Very low profile.

name: Saravana Selvarathinam
current_role: Managing Director, Saravana Selvarathnam Retail Pvt Ltd (Saravana Selvarathinam stores, Chennai) per company-registry data
profile: Part of the Nadar family behind Chennai's Saravana Stores retail empire (founded 1969 as 'Shanmugam Stores', a vessel shop, by brothers Yogarathinam, Selvarathinam and Rajarathinam). The 'Saravana Selvarathinam' branch, founded by S. Selvarathinam, runs large stores in T. Nagar and Pallavaram (Chennai), Tirunelveli and Madurai; registry data lists 'Selvarathinam Saravana' as MD of its retail company.
interesting_fact: Saravana Stores began as 'Shanmugam Stores', a small shop selling vessels, before opening its first big 'Saravana Stores' complex in T. Nagar in 1977; the family's founders came from Panika Nadar Kudiyiruppu village near Tuticorin.
notes: Identity uncertain: Hurun name may refer to the Selvarathinam branch/family or to the son listed in registries as 'Selvarathinam Saravana' (DIN 01835364). Company site saravanaonline.com was unreachable; no published contact found. Very low media profile.

name: Victoria Valenzuela
current_role: Director, AppLovin Corp (nominated 2026 after retiring as Chief Administrative & Legal Officer on Aug 1, 2026); consultant to AppLovin through May 2027
profile: Victoria 'Tory' Valenzuela was AppLovin's Chief Legal Officer and Corporate Secretary from May 2020 (later Chief Administrative & Legal Officer), joining via AppLovin's acquisition of Machine Zone, where she was CLO from 2015. She guided AppLovin through its 2021 IPO and hypergrowth, retired from management in Aug 2026 and was put forward for the board.
interesting_fact: CEO Adam Foroughi credited her with 'helping guide the Company through its IPO and a period of rapid expansion' when announcing her move from the C-suite to the boardroom in April 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech gaming she spent a decade (2004-2014) as General Counsel and Corporate Secretary of chipmaker Cypress Semiconductor, after starting as a corporate/tech lawyer at Brobeck, Phleger & Harrison and Clifford Chance; she holds a B.A. from Cal State Fullerton and a J.D. from Stanford.
notes: Goes by 'Tory'. Recognized in 2022 by San Francisco Business Times as an Outstanding LGBTQ Business Leader (per AppLovin bio page https://www.applovin.com/?p=7610). Route via AppLovin press.

name: Kathy J Warden
current_role: Chair, CEO and President, Northrop Grumman; Director, Merck & Co.
profile: Kathy Warden has led Northrop Grumman as CEO since January 2019 and chair since July 2019, steering the defense giant behind the B-21 Raider and Sentinel ICBM programs. She began at General Electric, held executive roles at Veridian and General Dynamics, joined Northrop in 2008 and rose to president and COO before the top job.
interesting_fact: In 2022 Russia put her on its sanctions list; she told David Rubenstein the sanctions 'don't really accomplish anything, but - it's part of the job.'
deep_cut_fact: She grew up in Smithsburg, Maryland (near Hagerstown, pop. ~3,000) and joked 'I don't think we knew how to spell aerospace and defense in Smithsburg'; with no one to guide her, she researched colleges herself pre-internet and chose James Madison University for its teaching focus.
notes: Very high-profile Fortune 100 CEO; active on public speaking circuit (Economic Club, Brookings, KPMG). Best route is Northrop corporate communications. Energy/data-center angle: space and defense electronics.

notes: No verifiable current information found in English or accessible Chinese sources (Baidu Baike blocked from this environment). Check Chinese corporate registries for the group's current status. Very low profile.

name: David J. Rosa
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, Intuitive Surgical (since July 1, 2025)
profile: Dave Rosa has spent nearly all of Intuitive's history at the robotic-surgery pioneer, joining in 1996 as a mechanical engineer on the first da Vinci system. He later led engineering, regulatory, sales and marketing, served as chief business officer and president (2023), and succeeded Gary Guthart as CEO in July 2025.
interesting_fact: An engineer with multiple patents, he founded Intuitive's first clinical engineering and endoluminal groups, which led to the da Vinci single-port (SP) robot and the Ion bronchoscopy system.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Intuitive as a mechanical engineer working on the very first da Vinci system and has said he 'really loved' tackling its unique and complex engineering challenges; he is a Cal Poly San Luis Obispo mechanical engineering grad (B.S. 1989).
notes: Cal Poly degree per CSU alumni profile (https://calstate.edu/impact-of-the-csu/alumni/made-in-the-csu/san-luis-obispo/Pages/david-j-rosa.aspx). Speaks at DeviceTalks. Best route: Intuitive media relations.

name: A B Krongard
current_role: Director, Iridium Communications (since 2009) and Apollo Global Management; former Executive Director of the CIA
profile: Alvin B. 'Buzzy' Krongard (b. 1936) spent 29 years in finance, rising to chairman and CEO of Alex. Brown & Sons (the oldest US investment bank) and vice chairman of Bankers Trust after their merger. He then served at the CIA as counselor to the DCI and, from 2001-2004, as Executive Director (the agency's COO). He now sits on the boards of Iridium and Apollo.
interesting_fact: A former Marine Corps infantry officer, he went from running Wall Street's oldest investment bank to being the CIA's No. 3 official, effectively its chief operating officer, in 2001.
deep_cut_fact: A Princeton philosophy major (A.B. 1958, senior thesis 'The Nature and Meaning of Religious Propositions') and lacrosse player, he was inducted into the National Lacrosse Hall of Fame in 1980; its bio says he 'was captain of every team on which he ever played.'
notes: Turns 90 in Oct 2026; long-time Baltimore figure (Mount Washington Lacrosse Club). Very private; no personal channels. Iridium (satellite comms) angle may suit the podcast. Avoid 9/11-trading and Blackwater topics referenced on his Wikipedia page.

name: Patrick Miles
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Alphatec Holdings / ATEC Spine (since Oct 2017)
profile: Pat Miles spent ~16 years at spine-surgery company NuVasive, rising to president, COO and vice chairman, and helped build its lateral-approach and nerve-monitoring franchise. In 2017 he took over near-insolvent Carlsbad rival Alphatec and has rebuilt it into a fast-growing 'approach-based' spine company (2026 revenue guidance ~US$880-890m), including buying EOS imaging.
interesting_fact: He took on Alphatec in 2017 when it had shrunk after selling its international business to Globus to stay solvent, betting he could rebuild the culture and innovation he had helped create at NuVasive - a turnaround now guiding to ~$890m revenue in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: As part of NuVasive's senior leadership with Alex Lukianov and Keith Valentine, he helped pick the cheetah as NuVasive's emblem to symbolize its commitment to innovation and customer responsiveness.
notes: Bought ~$1m of ATEC stock in Sept 2026 (Form 4). Earlier career: marketing director at ORATEC Interventions (2000-01). Route via ATEC IR.

name: Lainie Goldstein
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Take-Two Interactive (since 2007); Director, Phreesia
profile: Lainie Goldstein has been CFO of Take-Two Interactive (Rockstar/GTA, 2K, Zynga) since 2007, after joining as SVP Finance in 2003; she oversees finance, accounting, tax, treasury, IR and corporate communications. A CPA, she previously was VP Finance & Business Development at Nautica and worked in audit and reorganization at Grant Thornton. She also sits on Phreesia's board.
interesting_fact: She has been CFO through nearly two decades of Grand Theft Auto releases - from GTA IV to the build-up to GTA VI - making her one of the longest-serving CFOs in video games; she stepped up (initially on an interim basis) in 2007.
deep_cut_fact: Before video games she worked in fashion: she rose through finance roles at apparel maker Nautica Enterprises to VP of Finance and Business Development; she earned her accounting degree at American University in Washington, D.C.
notes: Low personal media profile; communications routed via Take-Two IR/corporate comms (which report to her).

name: Haiping Dun
current_role: Independent Director, ACM Research (ACMR) since 2004; compensation committee chair / audit committee member
profile: Haiping Dun is a semiconductor veteran who spent over 20 years at Intel (1983-2004), retiring as a senior director, then led Taiwan-based IC company Champion Microelectronic Corp. He has served on the board of ACM Research, the Fremont/Shanghai maker of wafer-cleaning and semiconductor process equipment, since 2004 - well before its 2017 Nasdaq IPO.
interesting_fact: He has been on ACM Research's board since 2004, when it was a tiny startup; ACMR has since grown to roughly $900m in annual revenue as a key supplier of wafer-cleaning tools to Chinese chipmakers.
deep_cut_fact: A physicist by training: B.S. in physics from National Taiwan University, M.S. in physics from the University of Washington, and a Ph.D. in materials science and engineering from Stanford, before two decades at Intel.

public_contacts.value: The Blueshirt Group (ACM Research IR/media): steven@blueshirtgroup.co

notes: Low public profile; board-level only. Route via ACM Research IR (Blueshirt Group).

name: Rizwan M Jamal
current_role: Managing Director, Affiliate Partnerships, Affiliated Managers Group (stepped down as Head of Affiliate Investments Jan 2025); may have since fully retired
profile: Riz Jamal spent more than two decades at Affiliated Managers Group (AMG), the Florida/Boston-based firm that takes partnership stakes in independent investment managers, leading new investments and later serving as Head of Affiliate Investments. He announced his retirement in August 2024 and moved to a Managing Director, Affiliate Partnerships role from January 2025.
interesting_fact: AMG CEO Jay Horgen said Jamal 'has had meaningful impact across our commercial activities for more than two decades' when announcing his transition - he helped originate AMG's partnerships with boutique asset managers.
notes: Low public profile. Education (B.S. Boston College, J.D. Harvard Law) reported only by Comparably, unverified against primary source. Route via AMG PR.

name: Yadin Rozov
current_role: CEO, Ambac Assurance Corp & CIO, American Acorn Corp (since Sept 2025); independent director of Core Scientific (comp. committee chair), Dave Inc. and Oramed
profile: Yadin Rozov is a financial-restructuring and insurance specialist: UBS MD (Head of Americas, Repositioning Group), then a decade as partner at Moelis & Co heading Financial Institutions Advisory, then GoldenTree partner and CEO of Syncora Guarantee. He joined Core Scientific's board in Jan 2024 as it emerged from Chapter 11 and now runs Ambac Assurance.
interesting_fact: He joined the board of Core Scientific - the bitcoin miner turned AI/HPC data-center host for CoreWeave - on the day it emerged from Chapter 11 in January 2024, and chairs its compensation committee; he bought ~$1.2m of CORZ stock in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a scientist - a bachelor's with highest honors in physics and materials engineering from Rutgers, later an M.Sc. in data science from Columbia - and while at Moelis helped co-found fintech lender College Avenue Student Loans.
notes: Strong fit for data-center angle via Core Scientific board seat. Founder/managing partner of Terrace Edge Ventures LLC. Could also be reached via Ambac Assurance corporate communications.
